title: Imputation via Domain Adaptation: Rethinking Variable Subset Forecasting from Knowledge Transfer

problem.claim: Variable Subset Forecasting involves variables available during training being entirely missing during inference, creating a mismatch between complete-variable training data and partial-variable inference data.

gap.claim: Existing imputation methods transfer local knowledge but fail to capture essential global dynamics under distribution shifts.

contributions.claim: VIDA reframes Variable Subset Forecasting as cross-domain knowledge transfer and transfers variable-invariant knowledge from complete to partial observations through domain adaptation.
VIDA combines global time-frequency joint representation learning with Sinkhorn-regularized distribution alignment to bridge non-overlapping feature supports across domains.
VIDA jointly optimizes predictions on reconstructed and original data to enforce task-driven consistency for forecasting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across four real-world datasets, the authors report that VIDA outperforms state-of-the-art imputation methods by an average of 25% with partially observed variables.

narrative_sequence.summary: Variable Subset Forecasting removes variables at inference time that were available during training.
The resulting domain discrepancy disrupts cross-variable dependencies and global temporal patterns, while existing imputation methods primarily transfer local knowledge.
VIDA formulates the problem as domain adaptation and combines global time-frequency representation learning with optimal-transport distribution alignment.
The framework jointly optimizes predictions on reconstructed and original data to make transferred knowledge task-driven.
The authors report an average 25% improvement over state-of-the-art imputation methods across four real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Local imputation knowledge may be insufficient when missing variables disrupt global temporal dynamics and feature supports differ across domains.

interpretation.claim: Forecasting under variable absence can benefit from explicitly modeling invariant representations and aligning source and target distributions.

application.claim: For related partial-observation forecasting settings, consider combining global temporal-frequency representations, distribution alignment, and task-level objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported variable-missing forecasting setting or four datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablations, or computational requirements.
